name: Schist-Verdance
description: Schist-Verdance is a world of layered stone and rampant growth, where metamorphic rock formations thrust upward in foliated sheets and every exposed surface is colonized by aggressive vegetation within seasons. Mountain ranges display the characteristic banding of schist, silver-gray and deep green, while the valleys between them overflow with dense forest canopy. Geothermal vents along the rift zones create pockets of tropical warmth even at high latitudes.

The air is thick with the scent of growing things, chlorophyll and pollen and the dark loam of decomposition. Fauna rustle through the undergrowth in numbers that suggest a world operating at biological capacity, every ecological niche filled, every resource contested. Dawn breaks in chorus, hundreds of species calling simultaneously in a wall of sound that fades only when the canopy heats enough to drive the larger creatures to shade.

Schist-Verdance has never hosted intelligent life, a fact that puzzles xenobiologists given the planet's exceptional habitability and long stable history. The fauna show high intelligence in isolated species but no tool use, no language, no apparent drive toward civilization. Some researchers propose that the ecosystem is too efficient, too complete, leaving no evolutionary pressure toward the kind of scarcity-driven innovation that typically produces sentience.

The planet is a prime colonization candidate, but its intact biosphere has earned it protected status under interstellar conservation accords. Research permits are limited and strictly enforced, though the planet's sheer biodiversity ensures a steady stream of applications. Schist-Verdance represents something increasingly rare: a world that works perfectly without intervention, and the question of whether to leave it that way grows more contentious each year.
